action: Seqrite publishes indicators of compromise (file hashes, the C2 IP address and URLs, a certificate hash) in its report; hunt for them and apply Seqrite's detections.
date_note: Date of Seqrite's report; the page gives no earlier publication day. It says the phishing email was observed on 13 October 2026.
exec: Seqrite says a phishing email aimed at a Ukrainian regional government led to a commercial remote-access trojan, Azalea Agent, which it says is sold to multiple operators.
plain: Security firm Seqrite describes a phishing campaign against Ukrainian government bodies that used a fake military financial-aid letter to install a remote-access trojan called Azalea Agent.

key_findings: Seqrite says a phishing email was sent from a sm.gov.ua account to recipients on the Donetsk regional government domain dn.gov.ua on 13 October 2026, with a RAR archive named after a letter about redistributing a subvention for a military unit.
A shortcut disguised as a PDF downloads an executable that leads through several loader stages to the Azalea RAT.
Seqrite tracks the activity as an unattributed campaign and says it found no confirmed infrastructure overlap with previously reported clusters.
recommendations: Hunt for the indicators of compromise listed in the report.

sources.name: Seqrite Blog: From Phishing Email to Azalea Agent

summary: Seqrite reports a phishing campaign against Ukrainian government bodies, with an email observed on 13 October 2026 carrying a RAR archive built around a military financial-assistance lure. Its multi-stage chain ends in Azalea Agent, which Seqrite describes as a commercial malware-as-a-service tool available to multiple operators. Seqrite tracks the activity as unattributed.
title: Seqrite: phishing campaign on Ukrainian government bodies delivers Azalea Agent trojan

validation.note: Single source: Seqrite's own report, read in full; no second publisher read.

review.note: Compared 13 Oct email, domains, MaaS wording, unattributed status and IOCs with the Seqrite report
